title: Rabbi Chinena son of Rabbi Chananyah
author: Aharon Hyman
attribution: Model-assisted translation, editorially reviewed; publication authorized by Joshua Waxman.

paragraphs: Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin, end of chapter 7, relates that he was walking among the gufata of Tzippori and saw a sectarian take a skull and throw it up high; it came down and became a calf. He came and told his father, who said to him: “If you ate of it, it is a deed; if not, it is an illusion.” Hyman suggests that possibly his father is Rabbi Chanina, who was the head in Tzippori at the end of the days of the Amoraim in the Land of Israel.

notes.text: The saved Guggenheimer Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 7:13 tells the episode in the first person; Hyman paraphrases it in the third. Gufata is retained as the source word rather than asserting “hills” for an unsettled topographical expression. The father’s possible identity remains Hyman’s conjecture.
